description: The installation of 2no. padel courts under a canopy with floodlighting, on an existing Multi-Use Games Area including a small strip of adjoining land.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
REASON
To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the details shown on the submitted plans, numbers:
- 001 RevB Location Plan
- 002 RevA Existing Site Plan
- 003 RevB Proposed Site Plan
- 004 RevA Proposed Elevations
- 005 RevA Proposed Roof Plan
and shall thereafter be retained/maintained for as long as the development remains in existence.
REASON
To ensure the development complies with the provisions of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012), Part 2 (2020) and the London Plan (2021).
The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the following has been completed in accordance with the specified supporting plans and/or documents:
- Planning Statement prepared by Padel Tech Ltd and dated June 2026
- Heritage Statement prepared by SKR Lighting Design and dated September 2022
- Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment prepared by Ecology Partnership and dated April 2026
- Preliminary Ecological Appraisal prepared by Ecology Partnership and dated April 2026
- Noise Impact Assessment prepared by Peninsular Acoustics and dated May 2026
- Lighting Impact Assessment prepared by MEC Consulting Group Ltd and dated June 2026
- Flood Risk Assessment prepared by MEC Consulting Group Ltd and dated May 2026
- Arboricultural Planning Report prepared by Arb Consultancy Ltd and dated May 2026
Thereafter the development shall be retained/maintained in accordance with these details for as long as the development remains in existence.

Notwithstanding the approved plans, prior to commencement of works above ground level of the development hereby permitted, a landscape scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall include 29% Biodiversity Net Gain. The scheme shall include: -
1. Details of Soft Landscaping
1a Detailed planting plans (at not less than a scale of 1:100)
1.b Written specification of planting and cultivation works to be undertaken,

1.c Schedule of plants giving species, plant sizes, and proposed numbers/densities where appropriate, by taking into account the recommendations of the approved Biodiversity Net Gain assessment for a flowering lawn seed mix to be used which contains a diverse mix of low growing native wildflowers, resistant to more frequent management.
2. Details of Hard Landscaping
2.a Refuse Storage, including capacity
2.b Full details of the means of enclosure and boundary treatments, including product details with materials and fin

No above ground development shall take place unless and until a compliance statement in response to highest standards of fire safety of London Plan Policy D12 (A) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved statement and thereafter shall be maintained as such.
REASON
To ensure that the development meets Fire Safety Standards in accordance with Policy D12 (A) of the London Plan (2021).

No above ground development shall take place unless and until details of the type and treatment of the materials, which shall include finishes of dark matt colours, to be used on the exterior of the structure have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved materials shall be used in the construction of the development hereby approved, completed prior to its occupation/use and retained thereafter.
REASON

To enable the Local Planning Authority to control the development in detail in the interests of visual amenity and impact on the Conservation Area in accordance with Policies DMHB 1 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

No above ground development shall take place unless and until details of inclusive access to the development to meet the needs of people with disabilities have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities should be provided prior to the occupation of the development and shall be permanently retained thereafter.
REASON
To ensure that people with disabilities have adequate access to the development in accordance with Policies D5 and D12 of the London Plan (2021).

The Padel courts hereby approved shall only operate Monday to Fridays between the hours of 08.00 and 21.00, Saturdays between the hours of 08:00 and 18:00, and Sundays between the hours of 09:00 and 18:00, and at no other times.
REASON
To safeguard the amenity of the neighbours in accordance with Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Flood Risk Assessment prepared by MEC Consulting Group Ltd and dated May 2026. Prior to first occupation/use of the development, written confirmation that the approved SuDS measures have been implemented as part of the development as built must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence.
REASON

To ensure that surface water run-off is controlled and to ensure the development does not increase flood risk, in compliance with Policy EM6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 (2012), Policies DMEI 9 and DMEI 10 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), Policies SI 12 and SI 13 of the London Plan (2021), the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), and Planning Practice Guidance.

Prior to the first use of the development hereby approved, a comprehensive external lighting strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall strike an appropriate balance between human-centric needs and ecological protection as follows:
- Demonstrating that the lighting scheme provides safe and secure routes for pedestrians in and around the proposed development.

-  Assessing light spill and glare to demonstrate that the design incorporates mitigation measures, including Lux levels and colour temperature, with external lighting to be angled downwards, and light directed into the site, and it should not provide flood lighting to the adjacent trees to show consideration for any nocturnal species, as recommended by the approved Preliminary Ecological Appraisal prepared by Ecology Partnership and dated April 2026.
The approved lighting strategy shall be fully implemented prior to first use and retained in operation thereafter

The development hereby permitted, shall only be occupied by Padel courts falling within Class F.2 (c) (Areas or place for outdoor sport or recreation) as defined by the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), notwithstanding the changes to the Use Classes Order in relation to Use Class F. No other 'F' use class is permitted without seeking full planning permission.
REASON

To enable the Local Planning Authority to assess all the implications of the development on highway safety, parking and neighbouring amenities in accordance with Policies DMHB 11, DMT 1 and DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

All lighting associated with the padel courts shall be switched off no later than 30 minutes after the end of the permitted operating hours on each day, as specified in Condition 8 of this permission.
REASON
To safeguard the amenity of the neighbours in accordance with Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).
The development hereby approved shall be carried out in strict accordance with the approved Arboricultural Planning Report prepared by Arb Consultancy Ltd and dated May 2026.
REASON

To ensure that retained trees and other vegetation will not be damaged during construction work and to ensure that the development conforms with Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

Trees, hedges and shrubs shown to be retained on the approved plans shall not be damaged, uprooted, felled, lopped or topped without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority. If any retained tree, hedge or shrub is removed or severely damaged during construction, or is found to be seriously diseased or dying another tree, hedge or shrub shall be planted at the same place or, if planting in the same place would leave the new tree, hedge or shrub susceptible to disease, then the planting should be in a position to be first agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority and shall be of a size and species to be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority and shall be planted in the first planting season following the completion of the development or the occupation of the buildings, whichever is the earlier. Where damage is less severe, a schedule of remedial works necessary to ameliorate the effect of damage by tree surgery, feeding or groundwork shall be agreed

No earlier than three months and no later than six months following the first use of the padel courts, an acoustic verification assessment shall be undertaken by a suitably qualified acoustic consultant and submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing.

The assessment shall be undertaken during representative periods of normal operation and shall include monitoring during a period when both padel courts are simultaneously in use for a continuous period sufficient to provide representative data, including during the public hire of the courts outside normal school hours.

The assessment shall include measurements at locations representative of the nearest noise-sensitive residential receptors and shall demonstrate compliance with the noise levels, assumptions and conclusions contained within the approved Acoustic Assessment prepared by Peninsular Acoustics Ltd, Project PA1820, May 2026, including consideration of both LAeq,1hr and LAFmax noise levels. open_spaces_details.description: The area of the existing MUGA is 575 sqm.  This will be replaced by two padel courts that will have an area of 497 sqm. The padel courts will be positioned side-by-side in an east-west orientation and will extend over a small area of adjoining grassland.  The area of adjoining grassland measures 125 sqm.  To compensate for this loss of open space (as suggested by the pre-app response) the surplus area of MUGA (170 sqm) will be landscaped to meet BNG requirements.  The net effect will be to create an additional 45 sqm of green open space
